decisions.summary: A caption declares its text and subject (group membership or data-names ids). A one-time migration strips its x/y and hand leader from the tracked sheet and writes the ids from today's subject reading.
decisions.why: This is the proposal the GM accepted ('a sheet declaring only a caption's text and what it names') and FR-002 ('nothing that decides where it stands'). The migration reads position once, only so that no caption changes what it names. Placement never depends on it afterwards. Unchanged since round 1.

decisions.summary: Inside or beside is the placer's call: inside seats first, then the ranked beside seats. Done in seat_label as two place() calls.
decisions.why: FR-002: the placer decides inside or beside from the drawing, and the sheet declares neither. Unchanged since round 1.

decisions.summary: The extended fallback (a whole-extent inside sample, slid point positions, a per-block search on stepped buildings) goes in labels/placer.py and is shared with the generated maps. It runs only when the standard search finds no free seat, and it is measured on the scripted maps.
decisions.why: The accepted proposal ('improve the placer's fallback'), the GM's 'reuse the same literal code', FR-003 ('improved in the placer itself') and the Assumptions all call for this. Unchanged since round 1.

decisions.summary: Mixed-size captions are measured and written line by line, at each line's own size.
decisions.why: FR-003: two of the eight measured misses have this cause. Any effect on the generated maps is covered by D9's before-and-after comparison. Unchanged since round 1.

decisions.summary: hand_sheet.placed() (D10) in each hand sheet's gen renders the PNG and the page from the placed text. make sheet-render renders any sheet placed.
decisions.why: FR-001: placing is a step of the pipeline and there is no separate tool to run. sheet-render is that same pipeline, offered to readers. Unchanged since round 1. Round 3: the function is now named hand_sheet.placed (D10). Only the name changed.

decisions.summary: Removes test_hand_sheet_captions.py, the caption ledger, make seat-label and its judge report, the four sheet-audit checks with their red fixtures and tests, the label half of trees_overlap, and building-review's caption-seat step. The tree's checks against the hand-drawn things stay.
decisions.why: The round 1 finding is resolved. The label half of trees_overlap (shared.py:410, the plan.labels line in _things_under_a_tree) is now on the removal list, and the stated reason matches the GM's ('There is no point in having an automated check run against an automated process'). What stays is a canopy against buildings, fences, wells, glyphs and tubs. Those are drawn by hand, and FR-004 keeps checks of things still drawn by hand. The rest of trees_overlap (walls, dividers, furniture, the duplicate-tree rule) is not named in the parenthetical, but D6 removes only what it lists, so it stays too. Every other sheet-audit reader of label positions was re-checked: occluded_foreground, orphan_group_labels, dark_on_dark_labels and overlapping_labels are on the list. labels.py pairing and the notice-board fallback are FR-005 readers, and D7 covers them. shared.py:87 reads text only. Every check of caption placement is now removed, so the list narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: pack_audit/labels.py pairs items with structures by data-kind tags. Any other reader of caption coordinates moves to the placed text or the tags.
decisions.why: FR-005. Since the label half of trees_overlap is now removed under D6, the phrase 'moved to the placed text' can no longer keep a placement check alive.

decisions.summary: SKILL.md Mode A usage, buildings.md, research presentation 040's note that names make seat-label, and the building-review and size-audit contracts: a sheet declares text and subject, the pipeline places it, and the contracts judge wording, not position.
decisions.why: FR-006. The round 1 aside (presentation 040 names make seat-label) is now in the list. docs/make-targets.html also lists make seat-label, but that page is generated from the Makefile and make-docs.py --check gates it, so removing the target under D6 removes its row as well.

decisions.summary: make quick; the one-time SC-002 measurement in measurements.json; the scripted maps' captions compared before and after D3; make done; the blind test at hand-back, with the 18 legacy exhibits named as untouched.
decisions.why: SC-002 as a one-time measurement and not a standing check; XIII verification of a change to shared code; the hand-back line the round-2 MODE 1 ruling required. Unchanged since round 1.

decisions.summary: The seat_label module moves to l7r/diagram/labels/hand_sheet.py, beside the placer, because every sheet's gen now imports placed. make sheet-render runs its main.
decisions.why: This decides where the code lives, and the requested behavior does not change. Moving it next to the one placer serves FR-001 (placing is a step of the pipeline, and no separate tool is run) and the GM's 'reuse the same literal code'.

decisions.summary: data-names lists data-id values, not SVG ids, because the sheets give three court rects one shared id (precinct) that the pack audit reads.
decisions.why: FR-002: a declaration carries its subject, 'one of several like parts included'. Naming by a shared id would name the wrong subject, as INNER and OUTER COURT did when they named all three rects. data-id is the mechanism that makes the declared subject the true one. Nothing positional is read.

decisions.summary: In the leader index, a dark stroke with a half-width of 2 px or more (WALL_HALF_PX) is an obstacle, unless it is part of what the caption names.
decisions.why: FR-003: the fallback must place at least as well as the hand seats. A leader led across a wall from the far side names something the reader cannot reach, so this rule makes the placer's result as good as a hand seat. The own-parts waiver is the standard's ordinary rule that a subject's own ink does not obstruct its own leader. It is not a carve-out, and nothing in it reads a caption's hand position (leader_blockers takes the drawn strokes and own_parts from the declaration). It lives in the hand-sheet adapter that reads walls from the SVG, and seats are still chosen by place(). FR-003's 'in the placer itself' concerns the fallback search that the generated maps share (D3), and that stays in placer.py.

decisions.summary: A caption of several texts may take the standard's own two- and three-line layouts (layouts()) for each one-line text, one line first. Line breaks the sheet declares are kept.
decisions.why: FR-003: the placer's standard wrap is extended to multi-text captions, so the granary's and the tally office's names fit inside their buildings. A one-text caption already had this. The line breaks a sheet writes are content (the caption's text and lines, FR-002), not position, so keeping them narrows nothing.

decisions.summary: Placement order: captions that must stand beside first, then those that fit inside, then glyphs in a named ground, each tier in document order. Then a repair pass re-places a caption still covering ink, with one near neighbor lifted, and keeps the pair only when the caption is freer and the neighbor no worse. A lift tries only the standard's seats.
decisions.why: Nothing in the order or in the repair reads a caption's hand position. The code (hand_sheet.seat/order/repair/fits_inside) uses the declared parts' boxes, each caption's font size and face, the placed blocks, and each caption's index in document order. Captions carry no x or y (D1), and Shape.center is not used in placement. Document order is where a text element sits in the drawing's paint order, which is already structural (classify uses it for ground painted after the caption). It is not where the caption's text was left, so FR-002 and SC-001 hold. The placer still decides every seat (FR-002). The repair adopts a change only when it lowers cost, and every caption's first placement ran the full extended search, so limiting a lift to extended=False cannot make the result worse than the greedy pass. FR-003 is not narrowed.

decisions.summary: Three declarations are written by hand where the migration's reading found no subject. Hayakawa's 'river landing' names landing-steps. The alcove notes on Hayakawa and Ubame continue the reception's caption (data-cont). Ubame's three border captions name fox-border-1 and east-wall-1..3. Each is recorded in its map's notes.
decisions.why: FR-002 makes the sheet the place that declares a caption's subject, so writing a subject by hand is the ordinary authoring act FR-002 describes. It is not an exception, and the choice reads no hand position at placement time. Each subject is true to the drawing. The sheet's comment says the landing is the flight of gangi steps. The alcove notes read '& ancestral alcove ...' and '& lineage alcove', which continue 'reception (zashiki)' as text, and the sheet draws no separate alcove shape for them to name. For the border, the east wall and the border line are drawn at the same x=1070, and the sheet's own note says 'The east wall IS the Fox/Scorpion line'. So the wall is part of what 'THE FOX BORDER' names, and the subject is faithful. The recorded motive ('so their seats stand off the wall') is about placement, but the subject stands on the sheet's own statement, not on that motive. Like D1's migration, reading where the alcove notes stood happened once, only to keep what they name, and placement does not depend on it.
